traditions.name: Masoretic Text (MT)
traditions.definition: The standard authoritative Hebrew text preserved and pointed by the Tiberian Masoretes (8th-10th c. CE), featuring consonants, vowels (nikkud), cantillation (te'amim), and marginal notes.

major_manuscripts.name: Codex Leningradensis B19a
major_manuscripts.significance: Complete Tanakh, basis for critical scholarly editions (BHS, BHQ).

major_manuscripts.name: Aleppo Codex
major_manuscripts.significance: Most accurate Masoretic codex verified by Maimonides.

traditions.scribal_rules: Strict Sofer rules: ink made from soot and gallnut, parchment from kosher skins, exact spacing, prohibition of copying from memory, counting of words and middle letters.

traditions.name: Dead Sea Scrolls (DSS)
traditions.definition: Over 220 biblical manuscripts found at Qumran (c. 250 BCE–68 CE) demonstrating textual pluralism in the late Second Temple era.

traditions.name: Septuagint (LXX)
traditions.definition: Ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Scriptures begun in 3rd c. BCE in Alexandria, reflecting pre-Masoretic Hebrew Vorlagen and Hellenistic Jewish theology.

traditions.name: Samaritan Pentateuch (SP)
traditions.definition: Independent transmission of the Torah in Paleo-Hebrew script preserved by the Samaritan community, containing Mount Gerizim cultic additions and linguistic regularizations.

traditions.name: Aramaic Targumim
traditions.definition: Aramaic interpretive translations recited in ancient synagogues: Targum Onkelos (Torah) and Targum Jonathan (Prophets), capturing early rabbinic interpretations.
